jina: Discharge of functions and authority of President
maudhui: (1) Apart from complying with the provisions contained in this Constitution and the laws of the United Republic in the discharge of his functions and exercise of his authority, the President shall be free and shall not be obliged to take advice given to him by any person, save where he is required by this Constitution or any other law to act in accordance with the advice given to him by any person or authority. (2) If the Cabinet finds that the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office by reason of physical or mental infirmity, it may submit to the Chief Justice a resolution requesting him to certify that the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office by reason of physical or mental infirmity. (3) Upon receiving a resolution submitted to him in accordance with subarticle (2), the Chief Justice shall appoint a medical board of not less than three persons chosen from amongst experts recognized as such by the law governing medical practitioners in Tanzania, and such board shall inquire into the matter and advise the Chief Justice accordingly. (4) The Chief Justice shall, after considering the medical evidence, certify whether or not the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office by reason of physical or mental infirmity. (5) Where the Chief Justice certifies that the President is unable to discharge the functions of his office by reason of physical or mental infirmity, the office of President shall be deemed vacant and the provisions of this Constitution relating to a vacancy in the office of President shall apply.
